meetings.title: Arcadia Health: discovery call
segments: Hi Rosa, hi Imran. Thanks for joining.
Noah from our solutions team is here too.
Hi everyone. Apologies in advance, I have a hard stop, there's a board prep meeting right after.
Understood, we'll keep it focused.
Rosa, Imran, thank you for the time.
I'd like to understand your world first.
Rosa, tell me about patient experience at Arcadia.
Of course. Arcadia runs eleven hospitals and about ninety clinics.
Patient services is roughly three thousand people, including our call centers.
My team is responsible for understanding what patients are telling us and making sure it reaches the people who can fix it.
Who uses patient feedback today, beyond your team?
Clinic managers, hospital operations, and our quality and safety committee.
The safety committee is the one that worries me most.
They get a monthly summary, and it's only as good as the sample my analysts read.
Before we go too far, I want to put one thing on the table, just so nobody wastes time.
Anything we buy has to support SAML single sign-on through Azure AD.
That's non-negotiable for our security committee.
Imran, do you use conditional access policies in Azure AD?
Some of our enterprise customers do.
Yes. Access is restricted to managed devices on our network or VPN.
Whatever you build needs to respect that, which it will if it's standard SAML.
Thank you for saying that up front, I really appreciate it.
SAML SSO is on our roadmap now.
I'll get you specifics on timing.
What else does the security committee look for?
A business associate agreement, because some of this feedback will contain patient information.
Clear data retention. And a detailed security questionnaire, it's about forty pages.
On retention, is there a specific period your policy requires?
For patient feedback, we keep it for seven years for compliance, but we'd want the option to delete earlier on request.
And any copies used for AI processing shouldn't be kept at all after processing.
That matches how our AI processing works.
Nothing is retained by the model provider.
We've done a few of those.
Send it over whenever you're ready.
Rosa, what does the feedback look like today?
Where does it come from?
Three main places. Comments from our patient portal, notes from the call center, and reviews of our mobile app.
Plus surveys after visits. It's a huge amount of text, tens of thousands of comments a month.
Are all of those in one system today, or spread out?
Spread out. The portal comments are in one database, the call center notes are in our contact center software, and app reviews we pull manually.
Getting them into one place would already be a big step for us.
And how do you make sense of it today?
Mostly by sampling. My analysts read a few hundred comments a month and write a report.
It's thoughtful, but it's a tiny fraction.
I'm always worried about what we're missing, especially anything related to safety or access to care.
For example, last year there was a problem with appointment reminders not being sent in one region.
Patients were complaining about it in the portal for weeks.
We only found out when a clinic manager escalated it.
How did that one eventually get fixed?
A configuration change in our scheduling system, it took an afternoon.
That's what hurts. It was an afternoon of work, and it took five weeks for the signal to reach the right person.
That's a really powerful example.
That's exactly the kind of thing we want to surface.
Noah, maybe a quick look at the themes view?
Sure. The idea is simple.
We take every comment, from every source, and group them into themes.
Each theme has a label, a count, a trend, and representative quotes, and you can always click through to the actual comments.
Can I see what a theme looks like when you click into it?
Sure. Here's a theme called 'Hard to reschedule appointments online'.
You see every comment in it, from every source, with the date and location.
And you can export the list or share it with someone.
This would have caught the reminder problem in the first week.
This is exactly what I've been trying to build with spreadsheets.
Can it separate by hospital?
Yes, any field on the feedback, like location or department, can be used as a filter on themes.
My question is where the text goes.
If a comment includes a patient's name or a medical record number, and you send that to an AI model, that's a problem for us.
And we'd want the option to keep certain sources out of AI processing entirely.
The call center notes, for example, are the most sensitive.
That's supported per source. You can connect a source for search and reporting only, and exclude it from clustering and summaries.
Many healthcare teams start that way and expand once they're comfortable.
Good. That gives us a way to start without the most sensitive data.
That's a fair concern. Today we redact emails and phone numbers before any text reaches the model.
For healthcare customers, we'd want to extend that to names and record numbers.
I'll confirm the plan with our product team and follow up in writing.
That would need to be in place before we send real patient data.
I'd want to see it.
Understood. Rosa, can I ask about budget and timing?
We have budget approved for a patient feedback platform this year, a bit over one hundred and fifty thousand.
We'd want to go live in the first quarter.
The decision goes through our CIO and the security committee, and then procurement.
What would make this a clear win for your CIO?
Two things. Coverage, meaning we read every comment, not a sample.
And speed, meaning a safety-related pattern reaches the committee in days, not months.
If we can show both in a pilot, the CIO will support it.
Would a pilot on one hospital make sense, rather than all eleven?
Yes, that's how we'd want to do it.
One hospital, two or three months, then expand if the results are there.
Our largest site would be the natural choice, it has the most feedback.
And a single hospital keeps the security review scope smaller, which helps us too.
That's a great way to start.
I'll put a pilot proposal together once we've been through the security questionnaire.
Is anyone else in the running?
Our current survey vendor is pitching an add-on.
Honestly, it's not great, but it's the easy option because they're already approved.
That's helpful context. So next steps.
I'll send the SSO timeline and our BAA template.
Imran, if you can send the security questionnaire, we'll start on it.
And let's schedule a technical deep dive with your team and our integrations lead.
I'll send the questionnaire today.
Thank you both. This is the first tool I've seen that could actually replace the sampling.
